## Framing first

The brief frames "engine" as a roster property and preflight as a network question. Two unlisted options: (a) a hybrid transport — `--input-format stream-json` on stdin (no 32 KB argv limit, no cmd quoting) with `--output-format json` (one result object, no JSONL parser); you lose init/step diagnostics and the init conversation_id cross-check, so stream-json output is still the better default; (b) skip the credential preflight entirely and let the first real turn prove auth (the classifier already handles auth failures) — that keeps the hook network-free but weakens fails-closed. To choose between these I would need: whether `--sandbox` blocks writes (not just terminal/reads), whether `--print-timeout 0` really means infinite, whether `result` ever omits `structured_output`/`conversation_id` on SUCCESS, and how fast a resumed conversation's input tokens grow.

Live evidence in this task: `handoffs/04-agy-engine-design.events.jsonl` (a real agy 1.2.11 run) shows `conversation_id` at the top level of `init` but nested inside `step_update`, and no `result` event until completion — pin which event the parser reads.

## Q1

Stream on stdin is right (argv: 32 KB limit, quoting, and `--print` swallows the next token — a silent mis-prompt risk). Stream-path risks: the bridge must serialize the prompt into ONE NDJSON `user` line itself (PS 5.1 `ConvertTo-Json`, no BOM, CRLF escaped); `result` may be absent (kill/crash) while `init` already names the conversation; and `structured_output` can be absent with a non-empty `response` (F4), so the prose gate must stay mandatory.

## Q2

Record requested, send nothing, map to model-tier: correct. Rewriting the model id by effort would mutate the lineage and break parent matching. `panel: weighty` is not enough — it only affects panels; a solo `-Provider gemini` acceptance consult still lands on whatever model the entry pins. Add a second roster entry (e.g. `gemini-pro`) or purpose-based model selection.

## Q3

Fail closed, as proposed. Ingest-flagged hides a silent lineage break: the "new" conversation has no memory of the parent, yet would become the next parent. Fail-closed hides only the paid-for answer, and the design already keeps it named — correct trade.

## Q4

Default `new`, opt-in `resume`. The prompt already carries open findings and the brief, so `new` costs the judge little; resume buys continuity but grows the conversation (tokens, latency, contamination) with every consultation in the lineage, and panel members append asymmetrically versus codex members that fork.

## Q5

`agy models` in preflight: acceptable (one round-trip, fail-closed). In the hook: no — print `gemini: not checked` or use a TTL cache; the hook currently promises "no network call, about one second". I checked: no `cmdkey` target matching agy/google, no credentials file under `~/.antigravity` or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\agy` — I know of no network-free sign-in proof.

## Q6

Add to the classifier: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, `rate_limit_exceeded` → quota; `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, "not signed in", "login required" → auth; `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, "invalid model selection", "conflicts with --effort" → capability; `UNAVAILABLE`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, 5xx → transport. Note the current regexes match NONE of the SCREAMING_SNAKE codes, and `Get-RetryAfter` misses Google's "retry in 32s" (it knows "retry after" and "try again in") and gRPC `retryDelay {seconds}`.

## Q7

Conditions are right, plus: schema-validate the object (presence ≠ validity); require the resume conversation_id check; FAIL (not warn) on the conversation-not-found warning and on "partial output"/empty-response SUCCESS (F7); soft-denial can stay a warning but its text belongs in the ledger.

## Q8

`codex-findings -List`/`-Stats` and the scoreboard read the ledger's `reply` path and lineage — safe. Hardcoded: the repair original `$nn-codex-….original.md`, the header "# Handoff NN - Codex:", `$commandStr = 'codex ' + …`, pending-record notes, and `Get-CodexRule`'s name rule (`^codex(\.exe)?$`) which won't match `agy.exe` — recovery then depends entirely on the recorded launcher path.

## Q9

First: resume-mismatch (fake emits the not-found warning plus a new conversation_id; assert failed outcome, reply kept and named, nothing ingested, new id never parentable). Quoting: never pass the prompt through the `.cmd`; the `.cmd` only execs PowerShell, and `fake-agy.ps1` logs its raw stdin bytes; assert the logged NDJSON line, JSON-parsed, equals the composed prompt byte for byte (quotes, backslashes, `%APPDATA%`, newlines).

## Q10

D3 breaks the thread invariant as written (see finding #1); D6 breaks the hook's no-network behaviour (#2); D2's read-only claim is unverified (#3); D7's repair turn can silently land in a fresh conversation (#7). D4/D8 preserve all four invariants.

## Requested checks

- **RC1** (finding #3): in a scratch dir (workspace-write, 5 min): `agy -p= --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --sandbox` with a prompt "create file probe.txt"; the file's absence/presence settles whether `--sandbox` blocks writes.
- **RC2** (Q1/Q7): run 5 schema-bound agy turns (read-only, ~10 min); any SUCCESS `result` lacking `structured_output` or `conversation_id` forces the fallback conditions into D3.
- **RC3** (Q4): resume one conversation 3 times (read-only, ~10 min); record `input_tokens`/`cache_read_tokens` growth per turn to price default-resume.

findings.claim: D3's rule that any `warning:` or soft-denial stderr notice 'becomes a ledger warning, never a refusal' contradicts D4's fail-closed resume-mismatch rule: the F6 conversation-not-found signal arrives exactly as a `warning:` line, so any path that does not compare conversation ids (a result without one, or the D7 repair turn) would downgrade a lineage break to a warning and could ingest a reply from a brand-new conversation as if it continued the parent thread.
findings.trigger: A resume-mode agy run whose stored conversation was expired server-side: agy prints the not-found warning, answers from a fresh conversation, and the result's conversation_id differs from the parent.

evidence.reference: handoff D3 (lines 77-78) and D4 (lines 83-87), plus F6 (line 38)
evidence.observation: D3 mandates warning-never-refusal for stderr `warning:` lines; D4 fails the run only on the conversation_id comparison; F6 shows the not-found case is reported as a stderr warning and still exits 0.

findings.verification: With a fake agy that emits the not-found warning but a result whose conversation_id equals the parent, confirm the implementation still hard-fails (i.e. the warning, not only the id, gates resume runs).
findings.remedy: In resume mode, hard-fail on the conversation-not-found warning, on a missing result conversation_id, and on any id mismatch; keep other warnings as ledger warnings.

findings.claim: D6 puts an `agy models` network round-trip (up to the proposed 15 s timeout) into codex-providers.ps1, which the SessionStart hook runs at every session start; this breaks the hook's documented 0.3.0 contract 'No network call, no lock, nothing written ... about one second' and can stall session startup when the network is slow.
findings.trigger: The plugin hook enabled and a roster entry with engine agy present, on a machine where api.googleapis.com is slow or blocked.

evidence.observation: The hook's header promises no network call and ~1 s cost, and it shells out to codex-providers.ps1 -Json, which D9 extends with agy credential rows.
D6 plans `agy models` with a 15 s timeout inside the providers listing, and D9 makes the hook list agy rows like any provider.

findings.verification: Time the hook with an agy roster entry and a blocked network (e.g. firewall rule); observe the session-start line arriving only after the timeout.
findings.remedy: Run `agy models` only in the consultation preflight; the hook and providers listing print 'gemini: not checked' (or a short-TTL cached result) for engine rows.

findings.claim: D2 asserts 'reviews are read-only' under agy `--sandbox`, but F8 verified only that reads still work; agy's sandbox is documented as terminal restrictions, and in 0.3.0 a working-tree change during a review is only a drift WARNING, so an agy reviewer that writes files would still produce a 'usable reply' — the read-only guarantee degrades from enforcement to detection.
findings.trigger: An agy reviewer whose tools write a file during a consultation (e.g. a 'helpful' fix) while --sandbox permits writes.

evidence.observation: Only file reads under --sandbox were verified; write behaviour is untested.
tree_changed_during_review only adds a WARNING drift line; it does not fail the run.

findings.verification: RC1 in reply_markdown: run agy under --sandbox with a prompt asking it to create probe.txt in a scratch directory and observe whether the file appears.
findings.remedy: Verify and document write behaviour; if writes are not blocked, fail agy runs whose tree fingerprint changed (or record sandbox:'unverified' and keep the drift warning explicit in the handoff header).

findings.claim: D4/D3 do not specify which event supplies the conversation_id or how to parse agy's inconsistent placement: in a real run the id sits at the top level of the init event but nested inside step_update, and a killed run has no result event at all, so the parser needs fixed rules and should salvage the init id as a never-parent diagnostic.
findings.trigger: A timeout-killed agy run: the events file contains init/step_update but no result, and recovery wants to name which conversation was live.

evidence.observation: Line 1 is {"event":"init","conversation_id":"fdc21ce2-...","init":{...}} while step_update nests conversation_id under step_update; the file has no result event.

findings.verification: Feed the real events file to the new parser; assert the thread is captured from init for diagnostics and that the run is failed for the missing result.
findings.remedy: Specify: result.conversation_id is authoritative for the thread; init.conversation_id must equal it (mismatch = failure); on a missing result, record the init id as thread_candidate, never a parent.

findings.claim: The current failure-class regexes match none of Google's SCREAMING_SNAKE codes (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT), 'not signed in', or 'invalid model selection', so those failures land in 'unknown'; and Get-RetryAfter's wordings miss 'retry in 32s' (it knows 'retry after N' and 'try again/resets in N') and gRPC retryDelay {"seconds":N} payloads.
findings.trigger: An agy quota rejection phrased 'RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Retry in 32s' — classified unknown with no retry_after, so endpoint health never records the reset window.

evidence.observation: capability/auth/quota/transport patterns contain none of the Google codes; the After regex requires 'retry[- ]after', the In regex requires 'try again|resets' before 'in'.

findings.verification: Unit-test Get-ProviderFailureClass and Get-RetryAfter with the Google wordings from Q6; all must classify and the retry ones must yield a reset time.
findings.remedy: Add the Google codes and wordings to the class patterns and a 'retry in <dur>' / retryDelay branch to Get-RetryAfter, per the Q6 list.

findings.claim: Beyond the D3/D8 file-naming list, several code paths hardcode 'codex': the format-repair original is always handoffs/NN-codex-<slug>.original.md, the handoff header reads '# Handoff NN - Codex:', $commandStr is prefixed 'codex ', pending-record notes say 'codex is being started', and Get-CodexRule's name rule (^codex(\.exe)?$) will not match agy.exe, so recovery of an interrupted agy run depends solely on the launcher-in-command-line rule.
findings.trigger: An agy run that is interrupted between the 'launching' and 'running' pending states: the next run's descendant scan finds nothing named codex and must fall back to the recorded launcher path.

evidence.observation: All four sites embed the literal engine string 'codex'; Get-CodexRule matches only the process name codex/codex.exe, the recorded launcher substring, or @openai/codex.
-List/-Stats resolve replies through the ledger entry's reply path, and the scoreboard keys by lineage — these are engine-neutral and safe.

findings.verification: Grep the scripts for the literal 'codex' in composed strings (filenames, headers, command prefix, pending notes, process rules) and run the interrupted-launching recovery test with fake agy.
findings.remedy: Parameterize the engine token in every composed name/message; extend the process rule to agy.exe (or match the recorded launcher generically) and always record the resolved launcher in the pending record.

findings.claim: D7's format-repair turn rides `--conversation <thread>`, but by F6 an expired conversation makes agy silently start a NEW conversation whose only context is the repair prompt — there is no 'last message' to convert, so the model will fabricate an object from the schema alone and the repair can 'succeed' with invented content.
findings.trigger: A resume-mode agy reply that needs format repair after the stored conversation expired server-side.

evidence.observation: The repair prompt asks the model to convert 'your last message'; F6 shows a not-found conversation silently starts a new one with exit 0.
The codex repair path is only eligible on a VERIFIED thread; the agy variant must add the same id verification after the repair result.

findings.verification: Fake an agy repair turn that returns a new conversation_id; assert the repaired object is rejected and recorded as a failed repair, not ingested.
findings.remedy: After the repair turn, require result.conversation_id == the repaired thread and no not-found warning; otherwise fail the repair and keep the prose original only.

verdict_reason: This is a pre-build framing consultation, so the verdict is advice: adopt the design with the listed fixes to D3/D6/D2/D7 before implementation.
unproven: Whether agy `--sandbox` blocks file writes (only reads were verified, F8).
Whether `--print-timeout 0` waits indefinitely as --help claims versus the documented five-minute default.
How often a SUCCESS result omits structured_output or conversation_id in real runs (F4 observed response/structured_output divergence once).
How resumed-conversation token counts grow per turn, which decides the default mode in Q4.
